name: Gabriel the Prefect
bio: Gabriel the Prefect was a high official and epigrammatist of the age of Justinian, in the sixth century AD. A portrait of a prefect named Gabriel at Byzantium is the subject of an epigram by Leontius Scholasticus in the same Book of the Anthology.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 208.

poems.title: Book XVI, 208: On Love Asleep on a Pepper-Castor
poems.author: Gabriel the Prefect
poems.text: Neither when asleep, nor when lifeless, nor at the banquet, is Love without a fire-scattering nip.
